discovery: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and giant tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO magnetic tunnel junctions

nominees.name: Shinji Yuasa
nominees.affiliation: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), Japan

motivation: In 1995 Miyazaki and Moodera independently demonstrated large tunnel magnetoresistance at room temperature in ferromagnet/amorphous-alumina/ferromagnet junctions. They turned spin-dependent tunnelling, a low-temperature curiosity since Julliere, into a robust quantum effect usable at practical conditions. In 2004 Yuasa realised the theoretically predicted coherent tunnelling through crystalline MgO barriers and obtained giant magnetoresistance ratios of several hundred percent, driven by symmetry filtering of Bloch states. Together these discoveries established the magnetic tunnel junction as the central element of spintronics. It became the read head of every hard-disk drive and the storage cell of spin-transfer-torque MRAM, which is now embedded in commercial CMOS chips as nonvolatile, energy-efficient memory. This is a rare case where a surprising quantum-mechanical spin effect became a mass-produced technology within two decades. It builds on, and goes beyond, the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance.
